doc.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Gene Norman's jazz radio show and moving from violin to clarinet and alto
summary: Hearing bebop and Shorty Rogers on the radio pulled him from violin to clarinet and then alto in twelfth grade.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: But I started, what six years old, I guess it was the start of the first grade, but when I was in high school, about the eleventh grade there used to be a DJ out here named Gene Norman, who has since become a record producer, and he had a show called “The East Side Show” and it was all jazz. And of course that’s the time that — the coast has always been big with Stan Kenton and Woody Herman because they were out here a lot of the time. But in addition to hearing that, Shorty had left Stan’s band and so I heard all of Shorty Rogers and the Giants and all those things. And he was playing all the Miles Davis things, the “Birth of the Cool” and all the bebop from New York he would play, the older Fats Navarro and Howard McGhee and of course Bird and Monk and all those people. So I found myself walking to my violin lesson whistling “Groovin’ High” and “Scrapple from the Apple.” And so the violin didn’t last too much longer after that. I had picked up the clarinet in junior high school. My dad gave me about a year’s worth of lessons and so when I got to high school I was in the concert band, the marching band on clarinet, and the orchestra on violin. But as time went on, then I picked up the alto in the twelfth grade just before I got out of high school. And the violin began to go down the tubes after that.
